title: Bounded complexes with essentially small homology form an essentially small class
statement: Let A be an abelian category with a derived category D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] which is locally small in a universe w. Let P be an isomorphism-invariant class of objects of A with a w-small family of representatives up to isomorphism. The bounded objects K of D(A) for which every H^n(K) belongs to P form a w-essentially small class.

source.place: Postnikov induction in det-brown-hypotheses-small, steps 11-13; Stacks Project 014A and 014B for isomorphisms of triangles and uniqueness of cones.

proof.text: Extensions of two essentially small classes are essentially small: choose representatives Y and Z and one distinguished triangle for every connecting map Z to Y[1]. Local smallness makes this a small family. The isomorphism-of-triangles theorem with first and third components invertible identifies every extension with a member of this family. The proof uses Mathlib distinguished_cocone_triangle₂ and isoTriangleOfIso₁₃.

For a fixed interval [a,a+n-1], induct on n. The empty interval consists of zero objects. The truncation triangle at b=a+n has its left object in the preceding interval and its right object isomorphic to H^b(K)[-b]. The latter is in the essential image of P under the single-term functor. The preceding extension count completes the induction.
The small union over a in the integers and n in the naturals contains every bounded complex with homology in P. Choose n at least b-a+1 for upper and lower bounds a,b.
